newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean tycoons plea for leniency in bribery trial.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean tycoons plea for leniency in bribery trial.

text.p: Three South Korea business tycoons charged with bribery in a case involving two former presidents pleaded for leniency at an appeals session on Thursday, witnesses and court officials said.
The three said they gave political funds to disgraced former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, not bribes.
The three said they would do their best to help the nation's economic development if given leniency on the charges of offering bribes to Chun and Roh between 1980 and 1993.

"I'm very sorry to you and the people for the troubles. I will devote rest of my life to the economic development and hope for a generous treatment," Hanbo Steel Corp honorary chairman Chung Tae-soo was quoted by court officials as saying.
Former Daewoo Corp chairman Lee Kyung-hoon and Jinro chairman Chang Jin-ho also requested leniency.
At the initial trial, Chung was sentenced to a two-year jail term, Lee a suspended jail term and Chang two years in jail.
But state prosecutors on Thursday continued to demand stern punishment for the men.

Former presidents Chun and Roh are also on a separate trial facing charges of mutiny and treason relating to a 1979 military coup and the army massacre of pro-democracy protesters in Kwangju the next year.
Their appeals session started on Monday. Chun were sentenced to life and Roh a 22-1/2 year jail sentence in the initial trial which ended in late August.

The two former presidents, who ruled the country from 1980-1993, have admitted to receiving millions of dollars of slush funds from business leaders, but maintained the money was taken as "political funds".
The panel of judges said the date for the next session would be set later.
